glosses: to drizzle (to shed slowly in minute drops or particles)
to dream (to see imaginary events in one's mind while sleeping)

examples.text:
Gnuśność, co twardym letargiem zasnęła,
Nie zna snów smacznych, mży za przebudzeniem.
examples.translation:
Sloth, which fell asleep in a stiff torpor,
doesn't know delicious dreams; it dreams after waking up.
examples.english:
Sloth, which fell asleep in a stiff torpor,
doesn't know delicious dreams; it dreams after waking up.

examples.text:
I gdyby stary ów Jan Czarnoleski
Z mogiły powstał: to by ją zrozumiał,
Myśląc, że jakiś poemat niebieski,
Który mu w grobie nad lipami szumiał,
Słyszy, ubrany w dawny rym królewski,
Mową, którą sam przed wiekami umiał.
Potem by, cicho mżąc, rozważał w sobie,
Że nie zapomniał mowy polskiej — w grobie.
examples.translation:
And if that old Jan [Kochanowski] of Czarnolas
rose from his grave, he would understand it,
thinking that he was hearing some heavenly poem
that rustles in his tomb from above the linden trees,
dressed up in the old royal rhymes
with the language he himself knew how to use centuries ago.
Afterwards, quietly dreaming, he would think to himself
that he hadn't forgotten the Polish language – in the grave.

examples.text:
Mżyłem coś w krwawych mgłach;... ceglane domy,
Drzewa gdzieś ciemne – trupa na wieżycy,
Na roztoczonych kościach gad łakomy,
Niby kłąb ciała – robactwa – oręży –
Śnił mi się – i gwizd rozwścieklonych węży.
examples.translation:
I dreamed something in bloody mists: brick houses,
dark trees somewhere – a corpse on a tower,
on the unfolded bones a hungry reptile,
as though a tangle of the body – the vermin – a weapon –
was in my dream – and the hiss of enraged snakes.

glosses: To shed slowly in minute drops or particles.

examples.text:

glosses: To pour slowly and evenly, especially oil or honey in cooking.

examples.text: The recipe says to toss the salad and then drizzle olive oil on it.

glosses: To cover by pouring in this manner.

examples.text: The recipe says to toss the salad and then drizzle it in olive oil.
She'll be right back, had to drizzle before we leave.

glosses: To carry out parfilage, the process of unravelling.

glosses: Very small, numerous, and uniformly dispersed water drops, mist, or sprinkle. Unlike fog droplets, drizzle falls to the ground.

examples.text: No longer pouring, the rain outside slowed down to a faint drizzle.
Stop drinking all of my drizzle!

glosses: A cake onto which icing, honey or syrup has been drizzled in an artistic manner.

examples.text:
April 19, 2013,Felicity Cloake, "How to Cook the Perfect Lemon Drizzle Cake" in The Guardian
Drizzle is not normally good news. Not when it's falling from the sky, not when it's replacing a decent helping of sauce, and especially not when it's found on a menu in close proximity to the words "balsamic vinegar". Deliciously sticky, sweet and sour lemon drizzle cake is the one, and very honourable, exception.

The rest of the day is spent trying to concentrate on ingredient labels, ordering supplies, baking some fairy cakes for a hen party and two lemon drizzles, one for a new baby and one for an old dear's birthday.
